subject: Post-call recap: cost / quota qualification + surge handling
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: cost / quota qualification + surge handling

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can lock economics and quota behavior: 

Call summary (from our side)
- Finlytics baseline: ~30M tokens / month (user-driven search + summarization).
- Expected peaks: product releases can push spikes up to ~10–12M tokens/day for 2–3 days, otherwise typical daily peak ~1.5M.
- Key asks: predictable unit economics ($/1M tokens), how we handle surge/spike traffic (rate limits, burst headroom), and overage terms + SLA on quota increases.

Open items for you to confirm
1) Baseline monthly tokens (approx): confirm 30M or update.
2) Target unit economics: you mentioned a target in the ~$700–900 / 1M tokens range — tell us the target you’d consider acceptable.
3) Release windows: confirm typical duration (hours) and expected concurrency during spikes.

What we propose (initial offer)
- Baseline price: $800 / 1M tokens for the first 30M tokens (month 1 pricing).
- Surge allowance (no-charge headroom): up to 20% of monthly baseline within short windows (defined as up to 6 contiguous hours), automatically tolerated without billing adjustments.
- Overage pricing: beyond surge headroom, overage billed at 1.5x baseline ($1,200 / 1M tokens) for usage within same month.
- Quota increase SLA: requests to raise monthly quota by up to 2x baseline — 48 hour turnaround. For sustained capacity above 2x baseline, recommend Reserved/Dedicated capacity (we can scope).

Example math (30M baseline):
- Monthly baseline cost: 30 * $800 = $24,000 (note: numbers expressed per 1M tokens).
- Allowed short surge (20%): up to 6M tokens for short windows no extra charge.
- If you spike +10M beyond surge headroom in a month -> 10 * $1,200 = $12,000 overage.

Attachments / links: attached MAP (mutual action plan) draft and a PO template for your procurement team. I’ve also added HubSpot deal link and a DocuSign placeholder in the metadata.

Next steps I suggest
- Elena: confirm the three open items above (baseline, target $/1M, release window lengths).
- We (Redwood): we’ll produce a revised MAP that includes the approved headroom, promotional credit options, and a suggested SLA for quota increases.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if it helps to walk through scenarios.

— Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments:
- MAP-Finlytics-2026.pdf (draft mutual action plan)
- PO-template.docx

From: Elena Torres <elena@finlytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finlytics Ops <ops@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: cost / quota qualification + surge handling

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Baseline: yes, 30M tokens / month is our current forecast for the next 6 months. Could grow if adoption goes well.
2) Target $/1M: we were hoping to get to ~$750 / 1M tokens as a target CEP (cost-expectation point). If you can be at or below that with a modest commit, that will make the finance team happier.
3) Spike profile: when we do releases the large spikes usually run 8–12 hours (overnight launch, heavy indexing and user activity). During those windows concurrency rises ~6–8x vs normal QPS.

Questions: 
- The 20% surge allowance seems small relative to our multi-hour release spikes. Is there a mechanism to buy predictable temporary burst headroom for a short window (e.g., pay a premium for a 6–12 hour elevated quota instead of paying 1.5x overage)?
- How do rate limits behave during spikes? Is there per-route throttling or a global token bucket? We want to avoid hard 429s during launch events.
- Can you share whether Redwood will consider a one-time onboarding credit / trial usage to validate integration before committing?

If you can send a couple of alternatives (e.g., paid short-window headroom vs repeated overage), that will help us model cost.

—Elena
VP Product | Finlytics
elena@finlytics.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: cost / quota qualification + surge handling

Elena — great questions, thanks. Below I outline two practical patterns customers use, with concrete numbers so you can model cost: 

Option A — On-demand overage (simple)
- Baseline price: $800 / 1M tokens (as noted).
- Surge allowance: 20% no-charge short windows.
- Overage: 1.5x baseline ($1,200 / 1M tokens).
- Pros: simplest, no upfront commit. Cons: expensive at scale for predictable one-off releases.

Option B — Paid short-window headroom (recommended for release events)
- Mechanic: buy temporary headroom by reserving a time-limited quota uplift for a predefined window (6, 12, 24 hours).
- Pricing example: 6-hour uplift of 4x baseline rate priced at a premium of 0.6x baseline for the uplifted tokens. 
  - Example: if baseline rate is $800 / 1M, the 6-hour uplift rate would be $800 * (1 + 0.6) = $1,280 / 1M for tokens consumed during the uplift window.
- Pros: predictable bill for release windows, lower than 1.5x overage if you plan and reserve.
- Cons: requires scheduling the uplift ahead of the window (we can accept up to 12 hours notice for small uplifts; larger/dynamic uplifts require Reserved capacity).

Rate-limiting / throttling behavior
- Per-route token buckets + global account token bucket. Short spikes are absorbed by per-route and prefix caching.
- If account-level sustained QPS would exceed the configured concurrency limits, requests will be throttled (429). During a scheduled uplift we widen both per-route and account buckets to avoid 429s.
- For unplanned spikes we automatically attempt a 30-second backoff retry strategy; if traffic remains high and you don’t want throttles, reserve the uplift.

Onboarding credit
- We can offer a one-time $15k integration credit to validate the integration (applies to first invoice). If you sign a short MSA / PO for baseline commitment we can convert that into a credit on the first bill.

Next suggested step
- If $750 / 1M is your target, we can present two commercial options: (1) commit to 36M tokens / month for a 12-month term -> bring price to $750/1M, or (2) keep 30M baseline at $800/1M and add paid uplift windows (6–12 hours) priced at $1,280/1M for uplift tokens.

I’ve CC’d Marcus (sales lead) to confirm whether we can layer an intro promotion. Once you confirm which flavor you prefer we’ll update the MAP and put a PO / SOW draft in DocuSign.

—Rachel

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: cost / quota qualification + surge handling

Elena — thanks for the quick responses. Confirming what we’ll put in the updated MAP / SOW: 

Agreed commercial summary
- Baseline: 30M tokens / month.
- Committed option (your target): if you sign for 36M tokens / month (12-month term) we can set unit price at $750 / 1M tokens.
- If you prefer to remain at 30M baseline: baseline price $800 / 1M tokens.
- Paid short-window uplift (recommended for launches): 6-hour uplift to 4x baseline capacity priced at $1,280 / 1M tokens for uplift tokens.
- Surge allowance: automatic 20% short-window tolerance for small bursts.
- Overage (unreserved, after surge): $1,200 / 1M tokens.
- One-time incentives: $15k onboarding credit + 30% credit on first invoice overages (Marcus approved).
- Quota increase SLA: up to 2x baseline within 48 hours with advance notice; sustained >2x requires reserved capacity planning.
- Rate limiting: per-route + global token buckets; scheduled uplifts expand buckets to avoid 429s.

Next actions
1) I’ll update the MAP and put the SOW/PO template into DocuSign (link in related_links).
2) If you choose the committed 36M option, sign the SOW/PO and we’ll apply $750 unit price and the onboarding credit.
3) For launches, send uplift windows at least 12 hours ahead for small uplifts (we can accept down to 6 hours notice for 6-hour windows).

If that looks correct I’ll send the DocuSign and final MAP. Happy to hop on a follow-up if procurement wants to go through the PO template line-by-line.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Finlytics live.

— Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
